source: NIST X-Ray Mass Attenuation Coefficients (Hubbell & Seltzer, NISTIR 5632); element tables and table 2 tissue compositions
model: mu(E) = (mu/rho)(E) * rho, mixture rule over mass fractions. Monoenergetic: no beam hardening, no scatter.

enamel.label: Enamel
enamel.note: The most mineralised tissue in the body, and the reason a crown reads brighter than the root on any radiograph.
sources: Nanci A., Ten Cate's Oral Histology, 9th ed. — enamel, dentin and cementum as mineral / organic / water by weight, and their physical densities
Hubbell J.H. & Seltzer S.M., NIST X-Ray Mass Attenuation Coefficients (NISTIR 5632) — elemental mu/rho and the ICRU-44 tissue compositions

dentin.label: Dentin
dentin.note: The bulk of the tooth. The enamel-dentin contrast this produces is the single feature the geometry DRR should render BETTER than the volume, where partial-volume averaging at 0.16 mm softens it.
sources: Nanci A., Ten Cate's Oral Histology, 9th ed. — enamel, dentin and cementum as mineral / organic / water by weight, and their physical densities
Hubbell J.H. & Seltzer S.M., NIST X-Ray Mass Attenuation Coefficients (NISTIR 5632) — elemental mu/rho and the ICRU-44 tissue compositions

cementum.label: Cementum
cementum.note: Defined for completeness and NOT rendered in v1: 20-50 um at the CEJ is far below the 0.16 mm voxel, and it is barely denser than dentin, so it is radiographically indistinguishable from the dentin beneath it.
sources: Nanci A., Ten Cate's Oral Histology, 9th ed. — enamel, dentin and cementum as mineral / organic / water by weight, and their physical densities
Hubbell J.H. & Seltzer S.M., NIST X-Ray Mass Attenuation Coefficients (NISTIR 5632) — elemental mu/rho and the ICRU-44 tissue compositions

pulp.label: Pulp
pulp.note: Soft tissue in a mineral shell, so it reads as a radiolucency defined by what surrounds it rather than by its own attenuation.
sources: ICRU Report 44, Tissue Substitutes in Radiation Dosimetry and Measurement — cortical bone, soft tissue and adipose compositions, via NIST table 2
Hubbell J.H. & Seltzer S.M., NIST X-Ray Mass Attenuation Coefficients (NISTIR 5632) — elemental mu/rho and the ICRU-44 tissue compositions

pdl.label: Periodontal ligament
pdl.note: The thin radiolucent line around every root on the operator's own PA. Collagenous rather than generic soft tissue, but at diagnostic energies the difference is far below what the geometry error contributes.
sources: ICRU Report 44, Tissue Substitutes in Radiation Dosimetry and Measurement — cortical bone, soft tissue and adipose compositions, via NIST table 2
Hubbell J.H. & Seltzer S.M., NIST X-Ray Mass Attenuation Coefficients (NISTIR 5632) — elemental mu/rho and the ICRU-44 tissue compositions

gingiva.label: Gingiva
gingiva.note: Barely visible on an intraoral radiograph; included so a soft-tissue profile exists where the beam clips the arch.
sources: ICRU Report 44, Tissue Substitutes in Radiation Dosimetry and Measurement — cortical bone, soft tissue and adipose compositions, via NIST table 2
Hubbell J.H. & Seltzer S.M., NIST X-Ray Mass Attenuation Coefficients (NISTIR 5632) — elemental mu/rho and the ICRU-44 tissue compositions

corticalBone.label: Cortical bone
corticalBone.note: Used for the cortical plates and for the lamina dura, which is the bright socket wall outlining each root.
sources: ICRU Report 44, Tissue Substitutes in Radiation Dosimetry and Measurement — cortical bone, soft tissue and adipose compositions, via NIST table 2
Hubbell J.H. & Seltzer S.M., NIST X-Ray Mass Attenuation Coefficients (NISTIR 5632) — elemental mu/rho and the ICRU-44 tissue compositions

trabecularBone.label: Trabecular bone
trabecularBone.note: THE TUNABLE ONE. boneVolumeFraction is not measured from this patient; it is the parameter to fit against the operator's own PA in Phase 5. Note also that no trabecular PATTERN exists in the geometry model, only this bulk average — see the known gaps in docs/drr-plan.md.
sources: ICRU Report 44, Tissue Substitutes in Radiation Dosimetry and Measurement — cortical bone, soft tissue and adipose compositions, via NIST table 2
Hubbell J.H. & Seltzer S.M., NIST X-Ray Mass Attenuation Coefficients (NISTIR 5632) — elemental mu/rho and the ICRU-44 tissue compositions

zirconia.label: Zirconia (3Y-TZP)
zirconia.note: The crowns on 19 and 30. THIS SCAN CANNOT MEASURE THEIR DENSITY: the volume saturates at 3072 and 14-18% of each crowned molar is pegged there (CLAUDE.md 126), so 2500 HU locates the restoration cleanly and says nothing about how dense it is. The figure is the material's, from the literature — which is why this is the one tissue here tiered `schematic` rather than `derived`.
sources: ISO 13356 / manufacturer data for 3 mol% yttria-stabilised tetragonal zirconia polycrystal (3Y-TZP), the dental full-contour crown material — 6.05 g/cm3

air.label: Air
air.note: The background, and the reason an unexposed corner reads black.
sources: Hubbell J.H. & Seltzer S.M., NIST X-Ray Mass Attenuation Coefficients (NISTIR 5632) — elemental mu/rho and the ICRU-44 tissue compositions
